plan.overview: This one-day itinerary captures the perfect contrast between old-world spirituality and modern urban energy in Tokyo. You will begin with the serene atmosphere of Asakusa's historic temple district before transitioning to the world's busiest intersection and vibrant fashion culture of Shibuya and Harajuku, ending with a quintessential high-rise view of the city's glittering night skyline.
plan.weatherSummary: Tokyo weather varies greatly. Spring/Autumn are mild (15°C-22°C), while Summer is humid/hot and Winter is crisp/dry. Layered clothing and comfortable walking shoes are essential year-round as you will be covering significant distance on foot.

transportationGuide.overview: Tokyo features the world's most efficient rail network. Navigating is best done via Google Maps.
transportationGuide.recommendedPasses: Welcome Suica or Pasmo Passport (IC cards) for seamless tapping on all trains and buses.
transportationGuide.metroBusTips: Trains stop around midnight; avoid rush hours (7:30-9:00 AM and 5:00-7:00 PM) if possible.
transportationGuide.airportTransfer: Keisei Skyliner from Narita or Limousine Bus from Haneda are the most convenient routes to central Tokyo.
transportationGuide.rideSharing: Uber exists but is often just a taxi-hailing service. Local apps like GO or S.RIDE are more common for booking cabs.

packingAndPrepTips: Bring an IC Card (digital version on iPhone Wallet works best).
Carry a portable power bank for map navigation.
Keep a small bag for trash as public bins are rare.
Learn basic Japanese phrases like 'Sumimasen' (Excuse me) for navigating crowds.

days.title: Day 1: Tradition Meets Neon
days.summary: A full day spanning the historic depth of Asakusa to the electric pulse of Shibuya.

schedule.title: Senso-ji Temple Exploration
schedule.description: Tokyo's oldest and most iconic Buddhist temple. Walk through the Kaminarimon Gate and the Nakamise shopping street.
schedule.tips: Visit early to avoid the heaviest tourist crowds.

schedule.title: Lunch at Asakusa Unatoto
schedule.description: Authentic charcoal-grilled eel served over rice (Unagi).

schedule.title: Ginza Line Transit to Shibuya
schedule.description: Take the Tokyo Metro Ginza Line from Asakusa Station to Shibuya Station.
schedule.tips: Use the IC card to tap in and out.

schedule.title: Shibuya Crossing & Hachiko Statue
schedule.description: Experience the world's busiest pedestrian scramble and visit the famous loyal dog statue.
schedule.tips: Best view is from the 2nd floor windows of the Shibuya Mark City walkway.

schedule.title: Dinner at Katsu Midori Sushi
schedule.description: High-quality conveyor belt sushi with fresh seasonal catches.
schedule.tips: Arrive early as queues can be long.

alternativePhotos.caption: Shibuya Sky & Neon Skyline at Night

schedule.title: Shibuya Sky Observatory
schedule.description: Breathtaking 360-degree open-air panoramic views of Tokyo at night.
schedule.tips: Book tickets online weeks in advance for sunset slots.
